purpose: The table's parts and its markup-only root. Compose the anatomy by hand (`Table.Header` / `Table.Body` / `Table.Row` / `Table.HeadCell` / `Table.Cell`): the component owns markup, tokens, accessibility, column sizing (an emphasized principal column), sortable headers, selectable rows and a **freeze system** for sticky columns (an actions column) and a sticky header. The root is light: it frames the scroll viewport, the toolbar band (`title` / `toolbar` slots) and the `footer`, and loads no table engine. For repeated records pass `data` + `columns` to [`data-table`](./data-table.md) instead: DataTable renders through these same parts, and the context-aware toolbar parts (`TableSearch`, `TableFilter`, `TableExportButton`, `TableRefreshButton`, `TableLiveButton`) and the cell presets (`TableCellLink`, `TableCellId`, `TableCellStatus`, `TableCellTags`, `TableCellTime`, `TableCellActions`) go in its slots. Inside a hand-composed `Table` the toolbar parts have no rows to act on. **What the compound carries.** `@aziontech/webkit/table` attaches only the structural parts (`Header`, `Body`, `Footer`, `Caption`, `Row`, `HeadCell`, `Cell`, `SortButton`, `Toolbar`), so a hand-composed table costs what its parts cost. The toolbar controls and the cell presets compose `Tooltip`, `DropdownMenu`, `Popover`, `Input` and `CopyButton`; each is imported from its own entry (`@aziontech/webkit/table-search`, `@aziontech/webkit/table-cell-status`, …) and is not attached to the compound, so a screen pays only for the ones it renders. **Cell presets.** Six presets render the cells every list repeats, each inside a cell (or a DataTable `#cell-<id>` slot): `TableCellLink` (a name that leaves the screen: an optional muted leading glyph (`icon`) for the provider or resource type, a 12 px external mark on an address outside the app only (never on an in-app route), a tooltip naming the destination, underline on hover; optional `+N` overflow through `OverflowCount` and a copy button pinned to the end edge), `TableCellId` (an identifier with its copy button), `TableCellStatus` (one semantic `Tag`), `TableCellTags` (as many tags as fit, the rest behind `+N`), `TableCellTime` (avatar of the author plus a relative time that updates every minute, or counts from the nearest `WebkitProvider`'s `now`, the absolute time on the tooltip and for screen readers) and `TableCellActions` (the row menu named after the row). **Types** (declared in `injection-key.ts`, re-exported by `./table`): the column and slot types DataTable takes (`TableColumn`, `TableCellSlotProps`, `TableHeaderSlotProps`, `TableToolbarSlotProps`, `TableStateSnapshot`, `TableExposed`, `TableAppliedFilter`, `TableFilterField`, `TableDensity`), so a page can type its columns from the compound it already imports. Their shapes are documented in [`data-table`](./data-table.md).
useWhen: Use Table for records that share columns when you compose the rows by hand; for any console list of resources people scan, sort and act on, pass `data` + `columns` to DataTable, which renders through these parts.
A small, static table, or one whose cells need a layout the column model cannot express: compose `Table.Header` / `Table.Row` / `Table.Cell` by hand. The root loads no engine.
The parts of a DataTable: the toolbar controls and cell presets go in its slots, each imported from its own entry (`@aziontech/webkit/table-search`, `@aziontech/webkit/table-cell-status`).
Use Table for read-and-act content; for repeated records pass `data` + `columns` to `data-table`, and when people edit cells in place use `data-grid`.
avoidWhen: Repeated records with sorting, selection, paging, filtering, virtual rows or tree rows → use `data-table` (`data` + `columns`).
People edit many cells of many records in place, spreadsheet-style → use `data-grid`.
A short list of same-field rows added and removed inside a form (environment variables, headers) → use `attribute-editor`.
A short titled preview of a longer listing on a marketing page → use `listing-table-section`.
A feature-by-feature comparison of Azion with a competitor → use `competitor-comparison-section`.
Rows of mixed content (media, title, description, actions) that do not share columns → use `item`.
A grid of selectable cards or options → use `radio-group` with `type="card"`.
The same records as a grid of cards → use `card-list` (same collection, card layout).
related: `data-table` — the data-driven table (`data` + `columns`, TanStack engine) that renders through these parts.
`data-grid` — the editable, spreadsheet-like grid; a separate grid (`role="grid"`, one roving tab stop, in-cell editors) that shares these tokens, not built on these parts.
`pagination` — the page strip; put it in a `Table.Footer` in the `footer` slot.
`empty-state` — compose it in a full-width row when a hand-composed table has no rows.
`item` — list rows without a column structure.
`listing-table-section` — marketing section that composes a DataTable for a linked preview of a list.
bestPractices: Compose `Table` by hand only for small, static tables; for repeated data use `data-table`, which renders through these parts.
Mark the row-actions cell `type="action"` with `frozen="end"` so it pins to the trailing edge, and give the principal cell `principal` (or `grow="2"`).
Name the table: a `Table.Caption` labels it (`aria-labelledby`), or pass `aria-label` on the root.

Give `TableCellTime` dates from your data. Where the text must not depend on when it renders (an example, a test, a server render the browser hydrates), set `now` on the app's `WebkitProvider` and count sample dates back from that constant; never build them from `Date.now()` / `new Date()` in setup.
Import the root alone from `table-root`, or each part from its own entry (`table-row`), when only a few parts are used.
